changelog.change: Initial entry — the sequential, tick-through version of the nerve-block-guide framework (47-step run-through condensed into a 6-stage node walk + a tickable safety-rule checklist), for use during an actual procedure rather than as background reading. Companion to nerve-block-guide (framework/rationale) and last-lipid-rescue (full LAST detail) — dosing tables and the full LAST algorithm are not restated here.

purpose: A step-through run-through for an ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve block, from pre-procedure timeout to post-injection monitoring — the sequential-checklist companion to the nerve-block-guide framework. Use it as a pre-procedure rehearsal or a bedside tick-through, not as the place to look up dosing or the LAST algorithm (those live in their own modules).
entryPrompt: Walk the six stages in order. The LAST emergency sequence applies at ANY point — jump to it immediately if suspected, regardless of which stage you're in.

nodes.body: Confirm indication and target nerve(s); review weight, LA-class allergies, anticoagulation status, pre-existing neuropathy in the distribution. Calculate the maximum allowable dose in mg (weight-based) before drawing anything up. Confirm IV access is patent — obtain it first if not. Obtain and document consent (LAST, nerve injury, hematoma, infection, block-specific risks). Confirm Intralipid 20% is physically present BEFORE injecting anything. Confirm at bedside: airway equipment, BVM, O₂, epinephrine, benzodiazepine. Apply monitoring (SpO₂, continuous ECG, NIBP q2-3min). Position the patient. Run a formal timeout (identity, procedure, site, allergies, consent, emergency equipment).

Select the transducer: high-frequency linear (10-15 MHz) for superficial targets (< 4 cm); low-frequency curvilinear (2-5 MHz) for deep targets (> 4-5 cm). Non-sterile survey scan: identify the target nerve and adjacent vessels, activate colour Doppler over the planned trajectory, confirm nerve identity in both long and short axis (honeycomb fascicular pattern in short axis — tendons attach to muscle, nerves don't). Optimise depth, gain, focus zone, and anisotropy tilt before committing. Decide in-plane vs out-of-plane (in-plane preferred) and mark the skin entry point.

Open sterile supplies to the field. Hand hygiene, sterile gloves. Prep skin with chlorhexidine-gluconate in concentric circles from the centre out; let it fully dry (pooled chlorhexidine carried into tissue is a real risk). Sterile transducer cover with sterile gel inside it; sterile gel on the patient's skin. Draw up the local anaesthetic — verify agent, concentration, and volume against the pre-calculated dose, and label the syringe. Draw a separate 2-3 mL saline or D5W syringe for hydrodissection.

Re-image with the sterile cover on — confirm the nerve and a vessel-free trajectory. Raise a 1% lidocaine skin wheal (0.5-1 mL) at the entry point. Insert and advance slowly, tracking the tip continuously — do NOT advance if the tip is not visible; tilt or slide the probe until it reappears. If paresthesia occurs on advancement, withdraw 1-2 mm; never inject at a position that caused paresthesia. Once the tip is in the target zone, pause and confirm with hydrodissection (0.5-2 mL saline/D5W): correct spread separates the nerve from surrounding fascia; if fluid disappears without visible spread, reposition and repeat.

Aspirate 3-5 seconds — any blood return means withdraw and replan (negative aspiration does NOT exclude intravascular placement, up to 2% false-negative). If using epinephrine, give a 3 mL test dose and watch the ECG for 60 s for a HR rise > 20 bpm (unreliable on beta-blockade). Inject in 2-3 mL aliquots, aspirating between each, pausing 15-30 s between aliquots for early toxicity signs to appear; total injection time ≥ 60-90 s regardless of volume. Watch the US image continuously: correct perineural spread is a hypoechoic 'donut' around the nerve; nerve swelling on the image is intraneural injection — STOP immediately. High resistance (target < 15 psi) also means stop and reposition. If spread is unilateral or incomplete, withdraw partially, redirect to the opposite aspect, re-confirm tip position, and continue — don't compensate with more volume.

Maintain continuous monitoring for at least 30 minutes after injection — LAST can be delayed up to 30 min with perineural absorption. Reassess every 5 minutes for CNS symptoms (perioral numbness, metallic taste, tinnitus, visual change, confusion) and haemodynamic/respiratory change. Assess block onset at 10, 20, and 30 minutes: sensory (cold, pinprick, light touch) and motor, compared to the documented baseline. No sensory change by 30 minutes = likely block failure — reassess with US before proceeding with the primary procedure. Document the full procedure note and counsel the patient (expected duration, limb protection / fall precautions, return precautions).

nodes.prompt: LAST suspected — at ANY point in the procedure
nodes.body: Stop injecting immediately. Call for help — announce "possible LAST." Secure the airway, 100% O₂ (hypoxia accelerates toxicity). Treat seizures: midazolam 2-5 mg IV or lorazepam 2 mg IV — avoid propofol as primary seizure management. Intralipid 20%: bolus 1.5 mL/kg ideal body weight over 2-3 min, then infuse 0.25 mL/kg/min (double to 0.5 mL/kg/min if instability persists); repeat the bolus once at 5 min if no improvement; max ~12 mL/kg in the first 30 min. If cardiac arrest: CPR with REDUCED epinephrine (10-100 mcg boluses) — avoid vasopressin, calcium-channel blockers, beta-blockers, propofol. Cardiac recovery from bupivacaine toxicity can take 60+ minutes — consider ECMO early if available. Transfer to a monitored setting for a minimum 4-6 hours post-resolution (redistribution recurrence risk). Full detail: see the LAST — Recognition & Lipid Rescue reference.

checklist: IV access confirmed before the needle goes in — always
Intralipid 20% physically present at the bedside before the first mL — always
Total mg dose calculated, not just volume, against the weight-based ceiling
Needle tip visualised before every advance — never advance blind
Aspirating 3-5 s before every injection and after every reposition
Injecting in 2-3 mL aliquots with a pause between each
Injection pressure low and easy — stopped and repositioned if resistance was high
No nerve swelling seen on ultrasound during injection
No paresthesia, burning, or unusual sensation reported by the patient during injection
Continuous monitoring planned for the full 30 minutes post-injection
